premiere_or_publication: No complete performance in Bach’s lifetime; the earliest documented complete performance took place in 1859, and the first complete recording was made in 1929 under Albert Coates.
dating_note: Wikipedia: the composition was completed in 1749, the year before Bach’s death. Much of it is older: the Kyrie and Gloria went to the Dresden court in 1733 and a Sanctus dates from 1724, while sections such as the “Et incarnatus est” were written to complete the Mass in the late 1740s.

recording.why: Gardiner’s period-instrument recording with the Monteverdi Choir and English Baroque Soloists, made in February 1985 for Archiv.

trivia: Bach never heard the Mass in B minor performed as a whole, and its earliest documented complete performance came in 1859. Only five of its 27 movements are actually in B minor, and the “high” of its German nickname came from comparison with Beethoven’s Missa solemnis.
